league: Cedar Park Youth League · 8U Coach Pitch

skills.name: Ready Position
skills.why: Every play starts here. A good ready position means kids can move to the ball instead of reacting late from a standstill.
steps: Feet wider than shoulders, weight on the balls of the feet.
Knees bent, hips down — like sitting on a low stool.
Glove open and out in front; throwing hand nearby.
Eyes up on the batter / ball — chest stays tall.

mistakes.bad: Standing straight up with hands at the sides
mistakes.fix: Cue "Popcorn!" and have them drop until their glove almost touches the grass.

mistakes.bad: Bending only at the waist (hunched over)
mistakes.fix: Ask "Can you still see my shirt logo?" Eyes up keeps the chest up.

mistakes.bad: Feet together or crossed when they shuffle
mistakes.fix: "Don't let your shoes kiss." Practice slow side-shuffles first.

coach_drill.name: Popcorn Freeze
coach_drill.setup: Open grass. Whole team jogs or skips in a 15×15 area.
coach_drill.how: Coach claps and yells "Popcorn!" Kids freeze in ready position for 2 seconds, then jog again. Do 8–10 pops. Fake a clap sometimes — kids who don't bite get a cheer, not an out. Keep lines nonexistent: everyone moves at once.

home_drill.name: Living Room Popcorn
home_drill.gear: Glove (or bare hands), open floor space
home_drill.how: Parent claps "Popcorn!" while the child jogs in place or around the room. Hold ready 2 seconds. Add: after the pop, point left/right for two shuffle steps. Finish with 5 quiet "statue" holds.

skills.level_up: After popping, shuffle two steps the way you point, then pop again — without standing up first.

skills.name: Throwing
skills.why: Accurate throws get outs and keep teammates safe. At 8U, kids need a simple pattern: aim, step, throw over the top — not a push or sidearm dart.
steps: Grip: fingertips on the seams (two or four seam is fine); not deep in the palm.
Stand sideways; glove-side shoulder and glove point at the target.
Show the ball back (away from the head), step with the front foot toward the target.
Throw over the top; finish with the throwing hand by the opposite pocket.

mistakes.bad: Facing the target square and pushing the ball
mistakes.fix: Put feet on a line aimed at the target. "Look over your glove shoulder."

mistakes.bad: Stepping with the wrong foot (same as throwing arm)
mistakes.fix: Place a sock/cone in front of the glove-side foot: "Step on the sock."

mistakes.bad: Sidearm or stopping the arm at release
mistakes.fix: "Throw over a fence" and touch the opposite pocket after every throw.

coach_drill.name: Partner Target Lines
coach_drill.setup: Two parallel lines of kids, 20–30 ft apart (closer for newer throwers). One ball per pair.
coach_drill.how: On "Point!" kids freeze aimed; on "Throw!" they complete the throw. Rotate partners every 6 throws. Coaches walk the middle cueing — not long lines waiting. Extra coach = quick "fix it" station to the side for anyone struggling.

home_drill.name: Knock Down the Castle
home_drill.gear: Tennis/foam balls, empty cups or water bottles, a fence/wall target
home_drill.how: Stack a cup castle on a bench. Child uses Point-Step-Throw from 15–25 feet. Score: knock-downs. Step back after 3 hits in a row.

skills.level_up: Add a small crow-hop ("Scoot") before the throw, and finish balanced for 2 seconds.

skills.name: Crow Hop
skills.why: After fielding, a small crow hop loads the body so the throw to first has zip without arm-only effort. Keep it a scoot — not a long jump.
steps: Field the ball and bring it to the belly/chest.
Small hop forward; back foot lands sideways (skateboard stance).
Front foot steps straight at the target (usually first base).
Throw and finish to the opposite pocket; stay balanced.

mistakes.bad: Huge hop that throws them off balance
mistakes.fix: "Mouse hop, not kangaroo." Mark two shoe-widths and hop only that far.

mistakes.bad: Hopping before they have the ball
mistakes.fix: "No tock without a tick." Throw only counts after a clean field.

mistakes.bad: Hopping toward home instead of first
mistakes.fix: Lay a rope/line from fielding spot toward first: hop along the line.

coach_drill.name: Scoot to the Bucket
coach_drill.setup: Roller coach + pile of balls; laundry basket/bucket at "first" ~30–40 ft. Groups of 3–4 rotate in.
coach_drill.how: Roll a grounder. Kid fields, scoots, throws to the bucket. Next kid is already in ready. 4–5 reps each then rotate — never more than one waiting.

home_drill.name: Tick-Tock to the Chair
home_drill.gear: Glove, soft balls, laundry basket on a chair as first base
home_drill.how: Parent rolls grounders. Child says "tick" on the catch and "tock" on the crow-hop throw into the basket. First to 7 outs wins.

skills.level_up: Field a ball one step to either side, then crow-hop throw without resetting the feet first.

videos.title: Youth Baseball Drills: Throw with Crow Hop

skills.name: Catching
skills.why: Catching builds confidence. Start close and soft so kids succeed often; thumbs together for high balls, pinkies together for low balls, two hands always.
steps: Eyes track the ball all the way into the glove.
High ball: thumbs together, fingers up (like a window).
Low ball: pinkies together, glove down (bowl / alligator bottom).
Two hands: throwing hand covers / secures as soon as it hits.

mistakes.bad: Turning the head or closing eyes
mistakes.fix: Use a foam/tennis ball and start 6–8 feet away. Success first, distance later.

mistakes.bad: One-handing every catch
mistakes.fix: Only award a point when the bare hand covers. Scoring coaches better than lectures.

mistakes.bad: Glove flipping the wrong way (fingers down on a high toss)
mistakes.fix: Freeze before the toss: "Show me window or bowl?" Then toss.

coach_drill.name: Catch Ladder Partners
coach_drill.setup: Pairs with tennis balls across the infield grass.
coach_drill.how: Start close. Every clean catch = one step back; a drop = one step forward. 90 seconds, then new partner. Coaches float and spot-fix glove shape — no single-file line.

home_drill.name: Couch Ladder
home_drill.gear: Soft ball or rolled socks, glove optional
home_drill.how: Underhand tosses from a few steps away. Eyes on it + two hands. Step back on catches. Mix high (window) and low (bowl) on purpose.

skills.level_up: Catch 5 in a row, then take three giant steps back and try again.

skills.name: Fielding Grounders
skills.why: Most 8U balls are on the ground. Glove in the dirt out in front, top hand chomps like an alligator, then up to the belly — that sequence prevents "through the gate" misses.
steps: Start in Popcorn ready; see the ball off the bat / roll.
Move so the ball comes to the middle of your body.
Glove down to the grass out in front (fingers touch dirt).
Top hand CHOMPS on top; gather to the belt / belly.

mistakes.bad: Glove up so the ball rolls under ("through the gate")
mistakes.fix: "Glove eats grass first." Place a leaf in the glove they must show you before the roll.

mistakes.bad: Fielding between the feet / under the body
mistakes.fix: Put a cone a half-step in front of the toes: "Chomp it at the cone."

mistakes.bad: Reaching with the glove while feet stay planted
mistakes.fix: Roll slightly to the side and celebrate when feet shuffle first: "Middle!"

coach_drill.name: Alligator Wave
coach_drill.setup: Two coaches rolling; kids in two short lines of 3–4 (or a semicircle if one coach).
coach_drill.how: Roll straight, slow grounders. Kid chomps, flips back, goes to the end. Next kid is already ready. 8–10 reps each. No 10-kid single line — split groups.

home_drill.name: Fish in the Swamp
home_drill.how: Parent rolls "fish." Child is the alligator. Count fish eaten. Balls that get past swim to the ocean (parent scores). First to 10.

skills.level_up: After a clean chomp, crow-hop throw to a bucket "first base" for a bonus point.

skills.name: Fly Balls & Pop-Ups
skills.why: Pop-ups are scary at this age. Safety first: call it, get under it early, glove up like an umbrella. Start with balloons/soft balls before real baseballs.
steps: Find the ball early; call "Mine!" loud (one person).
Run to where it will land — get under it, don't drift late.
Glove up above the head like an umbrella (fingers to the sky).
Two hands; soft catch. If unsure, let it drop — no collisions.

mistakes.bad: Running with the glove already stuck up (can't see / balance)
mistakes.fix: Run with glove ready at chest; raise umbrella only at the last moment.

mistakes.bad: Two kids converging without calling
mistakes.fix: Rule: loud "Mine!" wins. Practice calling on every toss at practice.

mistakes.bad: Backing up flat-footed under a ball over the head
mistakes.fix: Teach a drop-step turn; use balloons first so fear stays low.

coach_drill.name: Umbrella Raindrops
coach_drill.setup: Coach with soft balls/balloons; kids spaced in an arc (not clustered).
coach_drill.how: High soft tosses one at a time to a named player. Everyone else freezes. Rotate names quickly so wait time stays short. Emphasize call + umbrella.

home_drill.name: Rainstorm
home_drill.gear: Balloons or soft balls, open yard
home_drill.how: Parent tosses gentle "rain." Child gets under and umbrella-catches. Count consecutive catches. Progress to tennis balls only when confident.

skills.level_up: Catch 5 raindrops in a row, then take one step farther from the tosser.

videos.title: How to Teach Kids How to Catch Fly Balls

skills.name: Hitting
skills.why: Coach-pitch success starts with a balanced stance, a simple load, and eyes on the ball. Tee and soft toss build the swing before live arm speed.
steps: Stance: feet wider than shoulders, athletic bend, eyes level.
Load / rock: hands and weight shift slightly back (quiet, not a huge step).
Stride soft toward the pitcher; swing level through the ball.
Back foot rotates — "squish the bug" — and finish balanced with belly button toward the field.

mistakes.bad: Stepping in the bucket (away from the plate) or falling over
mistakes.fix: Tee work with a line under the feet. "Squish and freeze" for 2 seconds after contact.

mistakes.bad: Uppercutting / eyes pulling off early
mistakes.fix: Tee at mid-thigh; cue "Eyes on the ball" through contact. Soft toss from the side.

mistakes.bad: Giant load that ruins timing
mistakes.fix: Shrink the load to a tiny rock. Rhythm: "Rock… step… squish."

coach_drill.name: Tee + Soft-Toss Carousel
coach_drill.setup: 2 tees + 1 soft-toss net/open space; groups of 3–4 per station.
coach_drill.how: 5 swings each, then rotate stations. Waiting kids shag or on-deck freeze swings (no live bats in the crowd). One coach per station; short lines only.

home_drill.name: Driveway Tee / Soft Toss
home_drill.gear: Tee or stacked bucket, wiffle/foam balls, bat, open space away from windows
home_drill.how: 10 tee swings with Squish the Bug. Then 8 soft tosses from a parent kneeling slightly off to the side (foam only). Freeze the finish each time.

skills.level_up: Call a target (up the middle / opposite field) before the toss and try to hit that gate.

skills.name: Base Running
skills.why: Outs at first often happen because kids slow down on the bag. Run through first, listen for the coach, and learn when to round vs. stop.
steps: On a ground ball to the infield: sprint hard — don't watch the ball.
Run straight through first base; break down after the bag.
Listen for coach: "Through!" vs. "Round!" vs. "Back!"
On extras: touch the inside corner and pick up the next coach.

mistakes.bad: Slowing down or stopping ON first base
mistakes.fix: Put tape/a cone 2 steps past first. "Break the tape." Race through every time.

mistakes.bad: Watching the ball instead of running
mistakes.fix: Drill with no fielders first — pure sprint on contact. Eyes on the base coach.

mistakes.bad: Rounding when they should run through (or vice versa)
mistakes.fix: Simple code words only. Practice both on purpose in the same station.

coach_drill.name: Break the Tape
coach_drill.setup: First base + a ribbon/tape held 2 steps past; or a coach with arms as the finish line.
coach_drill.how: Kids line up at home in groups of 3. On clap, sprint through first and break the tape. Jog back wide. Next group goes — continuous flow, ~15 seconds between groups.

home_drill.name: Mailbox First Base
home_drill.gear: A towel/base as first, chalk or tape finish line past it
home_drill.how: From a pretend home plate, parent says "Hit!" Child sprints through first past the line. Mix in "Round!" toward second sometimes. Time 3 reps and try to beat the best.

skills.level_up: Hit an imaginary ball, run through first, then quickly locate where the ball would be (point to it).

videos.title: Little League Tee Ball Baserunning Drill

skills.name: Game Basics
skills.why: 8U kids need a tiny playbook: where to stand, where to throw, what a force out is, and how to stay safe. Clear > clever.
steps: Know your starting spot (position cone) and face the batter in Popcorn ready.
Field it → throw to first unless a coach yells a different base.
Force out: when the runner must go, tag the base with the ball (feet on bag).
Safety always: helmet on in the box and on bases; bats only in the circle; stay in the dugout unless on deck.

mistakes.bad: Everyone chasing the ball (no one covers a base)
mistakes.fix: Freeze a play mid-demo: "Who has first?" Assign covers before the next rep.

mistakes.bad: Throwing to the wrong place in a panic
mistakes.fix: Default rule for new players: "When in doubt, to first." Celebrate that choice.

mistakes.bad: Swinging bats in the dugout / no helmet on bases
mistakes.fix: Team rule, enforced kindly every time. One reminder = sit one pitch.

coach_drill.name: Where Does It Go?
coach_drill.setup: Full infield spots with cones; coach with a ball (no bat needed).
coach_drill.how: Call a scenario ("Grounder to short — force at first!"). Kids field a roll and throw to the right base. Reset fast. 6–8 scenarios. Keep energy high; correct with one cue word.

home_drill.name: Kitchen Diamond
home_drill.gear: 4 placemats/shoes as bases, a soft ball
home_drill.how: Walk through force outs vs. tag plays with one "runner" (parent) and one fielder (child). Ask: "Where do you throw?" before each roll. End with helmet/bat safety quiz (3 questions).

skills.level_up: Child coaches the parent through one force-out play using the cue words alone.
